newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares close mixed on lower volumes.
newsitem.headline: KL shares close mixed on lower volumes.

text.p: Malaysian stocks ended the week on a mixed note as blue-chips saw some profit taking after fund managers locked in profits ahead of the weekend.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 leading stocks closed up 2.46 at 1150.18, after earlier hitting a four-and-a-half month high of 1,157.69.
Banks and industrials were among the most actively traded counters. "There was no follow through buying today after yesterday's exceptional buying activity," said one analyst.
The Second Board index was off 4.20 to 571.24.
At the close, 263 million shares were traded valued at 1,925 million ringgit. Losers outpaced gainers 316 to 265, with 142 stocks remaining unchanged.

"There was some institutional buying at the beginning of the day, followed by profit taking," said the head of research at Halim Securities. "But the selling was well absorbed by the market," she added.
Banking group DCB closed up 30 cents at 9.05 ringgit with 2.6 million shares traded. DCB's substantial shareholder Rashid Hussain Bhd hinted the bank had been in merger talks with foreign banks.
